quotes.quote: (i) a final judgment or final judgments for the payment of money are entered by a court or courts of competent jurisdiction against the Company or any of its Subsidiaries and such judgment or judgments remain undischarged, unpaid or unstayed for a period (during which execution shall not be effectively stayed) of 60 days, provided that the aggregate of all such undischarged judgments exceeds $10.0 million (excluding amounts covered by insurance), after notice to the Company by the Trustee or the Holders of at least 25% in aggregate Principal Amount of the Notes then outstanding voting as a single class;

quotes.quote: If any Event of Default (other than an Event of Default specified in clause (j) or (k) of Section 7.01) occurs and is continuing, the Trustee or the Holders of at least 25% in Principal Amount of the then outstanding Notes may declare all the Notes to be due and payable immediately. Upon any such declaration, the Notes shall become due and payable immediately. Notwithstanding the foregoing, if an Event of Default specified in clause (j) or (k) of Section 7.01 hereof occurs, all outstanding Notes shall be due and payable immediately without further action or notice.

In the absence of additional liquidity, the Company anticipates that its existing cash resources, with a continued focus on cash conservation, is sufficient to fund its operations into the third quarter of fiscal 2025.

quotes.quote: an adverse judgment against the Company in the trial with respect to Qorvo Inc. vs. Akoustis Technologies, Inc. DE Case 1:21-cv-01417-JPM , as described below under Note 14. Commitments and Contingencies (the “Delaware Trial”), would reduce the amount of time that the Company could continue operating with its current cash resources, and create an urgent need for additional liquidity or result in the Company’s curtailing or ceasing operations and seeking protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. steps.text: Notes: principal: $44.0M; judgment default: final judgments for the payment of money above $10,000,000 that "remain undischarged, unpaid or unstayed for a period (during which execution shall not be effectively stayed) of 60 days" (§7.01(i)), after notice by the trustee or holders of 25% of the notes
When it is decided: once in each stage of the dispute; paid 30 days after the stage begins
Decision date: P5 20 May 2024, median 3 Sep 2024, P95 22 Oct 2024 = when the decision falls, across the simulations that reach it

Projected available cash at decision date: P5 -$3.0M, median $1.9M = opening cash + projected operating flows from the bank data + the dispute's cash to that date, across the simulations that reach the decision
Amount owed at decision: median $68.5M, highest $69.0M = the judgment on this path (as entered, or as the ruling leaves it) + statutory interest to the decision date - amounts already collected

Settlement offer: P5 $0, median $0 = the company's available cash on the settlement date less its 30-day operating need, floored at zero and capped at the amount owed (30-day need: median $2.8M); paid as 12 equal monthly installments, the first on the settlement date (30 days after the decision) and one each month after; the claim is released on the settlement date; installments due after 10 Nov 2024 fall after the analysis period
The notes' judgment default (§7.01(i)) on the judgment as entered: 60 days after execution became available: between 16 Aug 2024 and 22 Aug 2024 (median 20 Aug 2024)

The notes' judgment default (§7.01(i)) if the judgment is final only on the post-trial ruling: 60 days after the court's order on the last pending post-trial motion: between 19 Aug 2024 and 6 Nov 2024 (median 18 Oct 2024)
The deadline to file a notice of appeal: between 19 Jun 2024 and 8 Nov 2024 (median 30 Sep 2024)
The notes' interest payment date: 17 Jun 2024: $1,320,000.00 due, paid in shares
Nasdaq's deadline to regain compliance with the minimum bid price: 21 Oct 2024
The earliest date the holders may file a petition (Indenture §7.06): between 15 Oct 2024 and 21 Oct 2024 (median 19 Oct 2024)

On the loan: through the company's cash. Slope debits each installment in full on its due date when the company's available cash covers it; a debit that fails stays past due and is retried on the next due date or month-end. Slope funds a draw only while nothing is overdue and no petition is filed

quotes.quote: as the Company cannot currently predict the results of the proceedings, no corresponding accrual has been recorded in the financial statements included in this Form 10-Q. However, a significant judgment against the Company in the Delaware Proceeding, which is currently in trial, would have a material adverse effect on the Company’s business, which could result in the Company needing to curtail or cease operations and seek protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. Any settlement of the Delaware Proceeding or other actions may also have an adverse effect on the Company’s business, financial condition and results of operations, including, but not limited to, substantial expenses, the payment of royalties, licensing or other fees payable to third parties, or restrictions on its ability to develop, manufacture, and sell its products.

quotes.quote: As of March 31, 2024, the Company had cash and cash equivalents of $ 15.2 million and working capital of $ 10.3 million. In the absence of additional liquidity, the Company anticipates that its existing cash resources, with a continued focus on cash conservation, is sufficient to fund its operations into the third quarter of fiscal 2025.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: an adverse judgment against the Company in the trial with respect to Qorvo Inc. vs. Akoustis Technologies, Inc. DE Case 1:21-cv-01417-JPM , as described below under Note 14. Commitments and Contingencies (the “Delaware Trial”), would reduce the amount of time that the Company could continue operating with its current cash resources, and create an urgent need for additional liquidity or result in the Company’s curtailing or ceasing operations and seeking protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. These matters raise substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern within one year from the date of this filing.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: The Company’s short-term and long-term liquidity requirements primarily arise from funding (i) research and development expenses, (ii) G&A expenses including salaries, bonuses, and commissions, (iii) working capital requirements, (iv) business acquisitions and investments it may make from time to time, and (v) interest and principal payments related to its $ 44.0 million aggregate principal amount of outstanding convertible notes and $ 4.0 million promissory note. Additionally, the Delaware Trial is currently in process. To the extent that the outcome of the trial includes judgments against the Company for significant damages or other relief, the Company’s liquidity will be additionally and severely constrained.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: as the Company cannot currently predict the results of the proceedings, no corresponding accrual has been recorded in the financial statements included in this Form 10-Q. However, a significant judgment against the Company in the Delaware Proceeding, which is currently in trial, would have a material adverse effect on the Company’s business, which could result in the Company needing to curtail or cease operations and seek protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. Any settlement of the Delaware Proceeding or other actions may also have an adverse effect on the Company’s business, financial condition and results of operations, including, but not limited to, substantial expenses, the payment of royalties, licensing or other fees payable to third parties, or restrictions on its ability to develop, manufacture, and sell its products.

quotes.quote: As of March 31, 2024, the Company had cash and cash equivalents of $ 15.2 million and working capital of $ 10.3 million. In the absence of additional liquidity, the Company anticipates that its existing cash resources, with a continued focus on cash conservation, is sufficient to fund its operations into the third quarter of fiscal 2025.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: an adverse judgment against the Company in the trial with respect to Qorvo Inc. vs. Akoustis Technologies, Inc. DE Case 1:21-cv-01417-JPM , as described below under Note 14. Commitments and Contingencies (the “Delaware Trial”), would reduce the amount of time that the Company could continue operating with its current cash resources, and create an urgent need for additional liquidity or result in the Company’s curtailing or ceasing operations and seeking protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. These matters raise substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern within one year from the date of this filing.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: as the Company cannot currently predict the results of the proceedings, no corresponding accrual has been recorded in the financial statements included in this Form 10-Q. However, a significant judgment against the Company in the Delaware Proceeding, which is currently in trial, would have a material adverse effect on the Company’s business, which could result in the Company needing to curtail or cease operations and seek protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. Any settlement of the Delaware Proceeding or other actions may also have an adverse effect on the Company’s business, financial condition and results of operations, including, but not limited to, substantial expenses, the payment of royalties, licensing or other fees payable to third parties, or restrictions on its ability to develop, manufacture, and sell its products.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: Except for the $ 48.0 million of common stock remaining available to be sold under its ATM Sales Agreement with Oppenheimer & Co. quotes.quote: Our Common Stock is traded on the Nasdaq Capital Market (“Nasdaq”) under the symbol “AKTS.” On May 10, 2024, the last reported sale price for our Common Stock was $0.57 per share.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies registration statement on Form S-3, 13 May 2024 (resale of note-interest shares)

quotes.quote: The Company’s short-term and long-term liquidity requirements primarily arise from funding (i) research and development expenses, (ii) G&A expenses including salaries, bonuses, and commissions, (iii) working capital requirements, (iv) business acquisitions and investments it may make from time to time, and (v) interest and principal payments related to its $ 44.0 million aggregate principal amount of outstanding convertible notes and $ 4.0 million promissory note. Additionally, the Delaware Trial is currently in process. To the extent that the outcome of the trial includes judgments against the Company for significant damages or other relief, the Company’s liquidity will be additionally and severely constrained.

quotes.quote: As of March 31, 2024, the Company had cash and cash equivalents of $ 15.2 million and working capital of $ 10.3 million. In the absence of additional liquidity, the Company anticipates that its existing cash resources, with a continued focus on cash conservation, is sufficient to fund its operations into the third quarter of fiscal 2025.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: an adverse judgment against the Company in the trial with respect to Qorvo Inc. vs. Akoustis Technologies, Inc. DE Case 1:21-cv-01417-JPM , as described below under Note 14. Commitments and Contingencies (the “Delaware Trial”), would reduce the amount of time that the Company could continue operating with its current cash resources, and create an urgent need for additional liquidity or result in the Company’s curtailing or ceasing operations and seeking protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. These matters raise substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern within one year from the date of this filing.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: The Company’s short-term and long-term liquidity requirements primarily arise from funding (i) research and development expenses, (ii) G&A expenses including salaries, bonuses, and commissions, (iii) working capital requirements, (iv) business acquisitions and investments it may make from time to time, and (v) interest and principal payments related to its $ 44.0 million aggregate principal amount of outstanding convertible notes and $ 4.0 million promissory note. Additionally, the Delaware Trial is currently in process. To the extent that the outcome of the trial includes judgments against the Company for significant damages or other relief, the Company’s liquidity will be additionally and severely constrained.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: as the Company cannot currently predict the results of the proceedings, no corresponding accrual has been recorded in the financial statements included in this Form 10-Q. However, a significant judgment against the Company in the Delaware Proceeding, which is currently in trial, would have a material adverse effect on the Company’s business, which could result in the Company needing to curtail or cease operations and seek protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. Any settlement of the Delaware Proceeding or other actions may also have an adverse effect on the Company’s business, financial condition and results of operations, including, but not limited to, substantial expenses, the payment of royalties, licensing or other fees payable to third parties, or restrictions on its ability to develop, manufacture, and sell its products.

quotes.quote: As of March 31, 2024, the Company had cash and cash equivalents of $ 15.2 million and working capital of $ 10.3 million. In the absence of additional liquidity, the Company anticipates that its existing cash resources, with a continued focus on cash conservation, is sufficient to fund its operations into the third quarter of fiscal 2025.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: an adverse judgment against the Company in the trial with respect to Qorvo Inc. vs. Akoustis Technologies, Inc. DE Case 1:21-cv-01417-JPM , as described below under Note 14. Commitments and Contingencies (the “Delaware Trial”), would reduce the amount of time that the Company could continue operating with its current cash resources, and create an urgent need for additional liquidity or result in the Company’s curtailing or ceasing operations and seeking protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. These matters raise substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern within one year from the date of this filing.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: as the Company cannot currently predict the results of the proceedings, no corresponding accrual has been recorded in the financial statements included in this Form 10-Q. However, a significant judgment against the Company in the Delaware Proceeding, which is currently in trial, would have a material adverse effect on the Company’s business, which could result in the Company needing to curtail or cease operations and seek protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. Any settlement of the Delaware Proceeding or other actions may also have an adverse effect on the Company’s business, financial condition and results of operations, including, but not limited to, substantial expenses, the payment of royalties, licensing or other fees payable to third parties, or restrictions on its ability to develop, manufacture, and sell its products.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: Except for the $ 48.0 million of common stock remaining available to be sold under its ATM Sales Agreement with Oppenheimer & Co. Inc., Craig-Hallum Capital Group LLC, and Roth Capital Partners, LLC, the Company has no commitments or arrangements to obtain any additional funds, and there can be no assurance such funds will be available on acceptable terms or at all.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: 5,000,000 of the Shares (the “Note Shares”) represent shares that may be issued, at our election, as payment of accrued interest on our 6.0% Convertible Senior Notes due 2027 (the “Notes”), as make-whole payments made in connection with certain conversions of the Notes or as payments made in connection with qualifying fundamental changes of Akoustis Technologies, Inc. (the “Company”)
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies registration statement on Form S-3, 13 May 2024 (resale of note-interest shares)

quotes.quote: Our Common Stock is traded on the Nasdaq Capital Market (“Nasdaq”) under the symbol “AKTS.” On May 10, 2024, the last reported sale price for our Common Stock was $0.57 per share.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies registration statement on Form S-3, 13 May 2024 (resale of note-interest shares)

quotes.quote: The Company’s short-term and long-term liquidity requirements primarily arise from funding (i) research and development expenses, (ii) G&A expenses including salaries, bonuses, and commissions, (iii) working capital requirements, (iv) business acquisitions and investments it may make from time to time, and (v) interest and principal payments related to its $ 44.0 million aggregate principal amount of outstanding convertible notes and $ 4.0 million promissory note. Additionally, the Delaware Trial is currently in process. To the extent that the outcome of the trial includes judgments against the Company for significant damages or other relief, the Company’s liquidity will be additionally and severely constrained.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: The trial is expected to go to the jury before the end of the week, and the jury is expected to issue a verdict in the next several days.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies fiscal third quarter 2024 earnings call, 13 May 2024 (machine transcript)

quotes.quote: However, if the jury adopts the theories of Corvo's experts, it is possible the jury will issue an eight-figure verdict. For that reason, this litigation may have a significant impact on the company. including its value, operations, and ability to raise money.

quotes.quote: As of March 31, 2024, the Company had cash and cash equivalents of $ 15.2 million and working capital of $ 10.3 million. In the absence of additional liquidity, the Company anticipates that its existing cash resources, with a continued focus on cash conservation, is sufficient to fund its operations into the third quarter of fiscal 2025.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: an adverse judgment against the Company in the trial with respect to Qorvo Inc. vs. Akoustis Technologies, Inc. DE Case 1:21-cv-01417-JPM , as described below under Note 14. Commitments and Contingencies (the “Delaware Trial”), would reduce the amount of time that the Company could continue operating with its current cash resources, and create an urgent need for additional liquidity or result in the Company’s curtailing or ceasing operations and seeking protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. These matters raise substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern within one year from the date of this filing.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: as the Company cannot currently predict the results of the proceedings, no corresponding accrual has been recorded in the financial statements included in this Form 10-Q. However, a significant judgment against the Company in the Delaware Proceeding, which is currently in trial, would have a material adverse effect on the Company’s business, which could result in the Company needing to curtail or cease operations and seek protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. Any settlement of the Delaware Proceeding or other actions may also have an adverse effect on the Company’s business, financial condition and results of operations, including, but not limited to, substantial expenses, the payment of royalties, licensing or other fees payable to third parties, or restrictions on its ability to develop, manufacture, and sell its products.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: Except for the $ 48.0 million of common stock remaining available to be sold under its ATM Sales Agreement with Oppenheimer & Co. Inc., Craig-Hallum Capital Group LLC, and Roth Capital Partners, LLC, the Company has no commitments or arrangements to obtain any additional funds, and there can be no assurance such funds will be available on acceptable terms or at all.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: 5,000,000 of the Shares (the “Note Shares”) represent shares that may be issued, at our election, as payment of accrued interest on our 6.0% Convertible Senior Notes due 2027 (the “Notes”), as make-whole payments made in connection with certain conversions of the Notes or as payments made in connection with qualifying fundamental changes of Akoustis Technologies, Inc. (the “Company”)
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies registration statement on Form S-3, 13 May 2024 (resale of note-interest shares)

quotes.quote: Our Common Stock is traded on the Nasdaq Capital Market (“Nasdaq”) under the symbol “AKTS.” On May 10, 2024, the last reported sale price for our Common Stock was $0.57 per share.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies registration statement on Form S-3, 13 May 2024 (resale of note-interest shares)

quotes.quote: The Company’s short-term and long-term liquidity requirements primarily arise from funding (i) research and development expenses, (ii) G&A expenses including salaries, bonuses, and commissions, (iii) working capital requirements, (iv) business acquisitions and investments it may make from time to time, and (v) interest and principal payments related to its $ 44.0 million aggregate principal amount of outstanding convertible notes and $ 4.0 million promissory note. Additionally, the Delaware Trial is currently in process. To the extent that the outcome of the trial includes judgments against the Company for significant damages or other relief, the Company’s liquidity will be additionally and severely constrained.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: The trial is expected to go to the jury before the end of the week, and the jury is expected to issue a verdict in the next several days.

quotes.quote: However, if the jury adopts the theories of Corvo's experts, it is possible the jury will issue an eight-figure verdict. For that reason, this litigation may have a significant impact on the company. including its value, operations, and ability to raise money.

steps.text: Event of Default (§7.01(i)): final money judgments above the threshold, excluding amounts covered by insurance, remain undischarged, unpaid or unstayed for the stated period, during which execution is not effectively stayed; it takes effect on notice by the trustee or holders of 25% of principal.

Acceleration (§7.02): on an Event of Default the trustee or holders of 25% may declare the notes due; a bankruptcy petition makes them due automatically; holders of a majority may rescind once every default is cured, and a judgment default is cured by payment, discharge or a stay.

steps.text: Fed. R. Civ. P. 62(a): "execution on a judgment and proceedings to enforce it are stayed for 30 days after its entry, unless the court orders otherwise."
Fed. R. Civ. P. 69(a)(1): a money judgment is enforced by a writ of execution; the procedure must accord with the procedure of the state where the court is located.
11 U.S.C. §362(a): a bankruptcy petition operates as a stay of any act to collect a claim against the debtor that arose before the petition.

quotes.quote: As of March 31, 2024, the Company had cash and cash equivalents of $ 15.2 million and working capital of $ 10.3 million. In the absence of additional liquidity, the Company anticipates that its existing cash resources, with a continued focus on cash conservation, is sufficient to fund its operations into the third quarter of fiscal 2025.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: an adverse judgment against the Company in the trial with respect to Qorvo Inc. vs. Akoustis Technologies, Inc. DE Case 1:21-cv-01417-JPM , as described below under Note 14. Commitments and Contingencies (the “Delaware Trial”), would reduce the amount of time that the Company could continue operating with its current cash resources, and create an urgent need for additional liquidity or result in the Company’s curtailing or ceasing operations and seeking protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. These matters raise substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern within one year from the date of this filing.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: as the Company cannot currently predict the results of the proceedings, no corresponding accrual has been recorded in the financial statements included in this Form 10-Q. However, a significant judgment against the Company in the Delaware Proceeding, which is currently in trial, would have a material adverse effect on the Company’s business, which could result in the Company needing to curtail or cease operations and seek protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. Any settlement of the Delaware Proceeding or other actions may also have an adverse effect on the Company’s business, financial condition and results of operations, including, but not limited to, substantial expenses, the payment of royalties, licensing or other fees payable to third parties, or restrictions on its ability to develop, manufacture, and sell its products.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: Except for the $ 48.0 million of common stock remaining available to be sold under its ATM Sales Agreement with Oppenheimer & Co. Inc., Craig-Hallum Capital Group LLC, and Roth Capital Partners, LLC, the Company has no commitments or arrangements to obtain any additional funds, and there can be no assurance such funds will be available on acceptable terms or at all.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: 5,000,000 of the Shares (the “Note Shares”) represent shares that may be issued, at our election, as payment of accrued interest on our 6.0% Convertible Senior Notes due 2027 (the “Notes”), as make-whole payments made in connection with certain conversions of the Notes or as payments made in connection with qualifying fundamental changes of Akoustis Technologies, Inc. (the “Company”)
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies registration statement on Form S-3, 13 May 2024 (resale of note-interest shares)

quotes.quote: Our Common Stock is traded on the Nasdaq Capital Market (“Nasdaq”) under the symbol “AKTS.” On May 10, 2024, the last reported sale price for our Common Stock was $0.57 per share.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies registration statement on Form S-3, 13 May 2024 (resale of note-interest shares)

quotes.quote: The Company’s short-term and long-term liquidity requirements primarily arise from funding (i) research and development expenses, (ii) G&A expenses including salaries, bonuses, and commissions, (iii) working capital requirements, (iv) business acquisitions and investments it may make from time to time, and (v) interest and principal payments related to its $ 44.0 million aggregate principal amount of outstanding convertible notes and $ 4.0 million promissory note. Additionally, the Delaware Trial is currently in process. To the extent that the outcome of the trial includes judgments against the Company for significant damages or other relief, the Company’s liquidity will be additionally and severely constrained.

steps.text: Event of Default (§7.01(i)): final money judgments above the threshold, excluding amounts covered by insurance, remain undischarged, unpaid or unstayed for the stated period, during which execution is not effectively stayed; it takes effect on notice by the trustee or holders of 25% of principal.

Acceleration (§7.02): on an Event of Default the trustee or holders of 25% may declare the notes due; a bankruptcy petition makes them due automatically; holders of a majority may rescind once every default is cured, and a judgment default is cured by payment, discharge or a stay.

In the absence of additional liquidity, the Company anticipates that its existing cash resources, with a continued focus on cash conservation, is sufficient to fund its operations into the third quarter of fiscal 2025.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: an adverse judgment against the Company in the trial with respect to Qorvo Inc. vs. Akoustis Technologies, Inc. DE Case 1:21-cv-01417-JPM , as described below under Note 14. Commitments and Contingencies (the “Delaware Trial”), would reduce the amount of time that the Company could continue operating with its current cash resources, and create an urgent need for additional liquidity or result in the Company’s curtailing or ceasing operations and seeking protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. These matters raise substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern within one year from the date of this filing.

28 U.S.C. §1963: a judgment may be registered in another district "when the judgment has become final by appeal or expiration of the time for appeal or when ordered by the court that entered the judgment for good cause shown." Good cause: thin forum assets and substantial assets elsewhere (Associated Bus. Tel. Sys. v. Greater Capital Corp., 128 F.R.D. 63, 66-68 (D.N.J. 1989)).

steps.text: Event of Default (§7.01(b)): the common stock is not listed on an Eligible Market; it takes effect without notice or grace period.

Acceleration (§7.02): on an Event of Default the trustee or holders of 25% may declare the notes due; a bankruptcy petition makes them due automatically; holders of a majority may rescind once every default is cured, and a judgment default is cured by payment, discharge or a stay.

Fundamental Change repurchase (§10.01): delisting lets each holder require repurchase at 100% of principal plus accrued interest in cash; notice within 20 business days, repurchase 20-35 business days after notice; failure to repurchase is an Event of Default.

quotes.quote: As of March 31, 2024, the Company had cash and cash equivalents of $ 15.2 million and working capital of $ 10.3 million. In the absence of additional liquidity, the Company anticipates that its existing cash resources, with a continued focus on cash conservation, is sufficient to fund its operations into the third quarter of fiscal 2025.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: an adverse judgment against the Company in the trial with respect to Qorvo Inc. vs. Akoustis Technologies, Inc. DE Case 1:21-cv-01417-JPM , as described below under Note 14. Commitments and Contingencies (the “Delaware Trial”), would reduce the amount of time that the Company could continue operating with its current cash resources, and create an urgent need for additional liquidity or result in the Company’s curtailing or ceasing operations and seeking protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. These matters raise substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern within one year from the date of this filing.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: Except for the $ 48.0 million of common stock remaining available to be sold under its ATM Sales Agreement with Oppenheimer & Co. Inc., Craig-Hallum Capital Group LLC, and Roth Capital Partners, LLC, the Company has no commitments or arrangements to obtain any additional funds, and there can be no assurance such funds will be available on acceptable terms or at all.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: as the Company cannot currently predict the results of the proceedings, no corresponding accrual has been recorded in the financial statements included in this Form 10-Q. However, a significant judgment against the Company in the Delaware Proceeding, which is currently in trial, would have a material adverse effect on the Company’s business, which could result in the Company needing to curtail or cease operations and seek protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. Any settlement of the Delaware Proceeding or other actions may also have an adverse effect on the Company’s business, financial condition and results of operations, including, but not limited to, substantial expenses, the payment of royalties, licensing or other fees payable to third parties, or restrictions on its ability to develop, manufacture, and sell its products.

steps.text: Event of Default (§7.01(i)): final money judgments above the threshold, excluding amounts covered by insurance, remain undischarged, unpaid or unstayed for the stated period, during which execution is not effectively stayed; it takes effect on notice by the trustee or holders of 25% of principal.

Acceleration (§7.02): on an Event of Default the trustee or holders of 25% may declare the notes due; a bankruptcy petition makes them due automatically; holders of a majority may rescind once every default is cured, and a judgment default is cured by payment, discharge or a stay.

steps.text: Indenture §7.06 (Limitation on Suits): "No Holder shall have any right to institute any proceeding, judicial or otherwise, in respect of this Indenture, or for the appointment of a receiver or trustee, or for any other remedy hereunder (other than in the case of an Event of Default specified in clause (j) or (k) of Section 7.01), unless: (a) the Holder of a Note gives to the Trustee written notice of a continuing Event of Default; (b) the Holders of at least 25% in Principal Amount of the then outstanding Notes make a written request to the Trustee to pursue the remedy; (c) such Holder of a Note or Holders of Notes offer and, if requested, provide to the Trustee indemnity reasonably satisfactory to the Trustee against any loss, liability or expense; (d) the Trustee does not comply with the request within 60 days after receipt of the request and the offer and, if requested, the provision of indemnity; and (e) during such 60-day period the Majority Holders do not give the Trustee a direction inconsistent with the request."

Indenture §7.07 (Unconditional Rights of Holders of Notes to Receive Payment): "Notwithstanding any other provision of this Indenture, the right of any Holder to receive payment of the Principal, the Redemption Price, or Interest, in respect of the Notes held by such Holder, on or after the respective due dates expressed in the Notes or any Redemption Date, as applicable, and to convert the Notes in accordance with ARTICLE 9, or to bring suit for the enforcement of any such payment on or after such respective dates or the right to convert, shall not be impaired or affected adversely without the consent of such Holder."
11 U.S.C. §303(b)(1): where the debtor has 12 or more creditors, an involuntary petition is filed by three or more creditors holding noncontingent, undisputed claims above the statutory threshold.

steps.text: Event of Default (§7.01(b)): the common stock is not listed on an Eligible Market; it takes effect without notice or grace period.

Acceleration (§7.02): on an Event of Default the trustee or holders of 25% may declare the notes due; a bankruptcy petition makes them due automatically; holders of a majority may rescind once every default is cured, and a judgment default is cured by payment, discharge or a stay.

Fundamental Change repurchase (§10.01): delisting lets each holder require repurchase at 100% of principal plus accrued interest in cash; notice within 20 business days, repurchase 20-35 business days after notice; failure to repurchase is an Event of Default.

quotes.quote: As of March 31, 2024, the Company had cash and cash equivalents of $ 15.2 million and working capital of $ 10.3 million. In the absence of additional liquidity, the Company anticipates that its existing cash resources, with a continued focus on cash conservation, is sufficient to fund its operations into the third quarter of fiscal 2025.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: an adverse judgment against the Company in the trial with respect to Qorvo Inc. vs. Akoustis Technologies, Inc. DE Case 1:21-cv-01417-JPM , as described below under Note 14. Commitments and Contingencies (the “Delaware Trial”), would reduce the amount of time that the Company could continue operating with its current cash resources, and create an urgent need for additional liquidity or result in the Company’s curtailing or ceasing operations and seeking protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. These matters raise substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern within one year from the date of this filing.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: Except for the $ 48.0 million of common stock remaining available to be sold under its ATM Sales Agreement with Oppenheimer & Co. Inc., Craig-Hallum Capital Group LLC, and Roth Capital Partners, LLC, the Company has no commitments or arrangements to obtain any additional funds, and there can be no assurance such funds will be available on acceptable terms or at all.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: as the Company cannot currently predict the results of the proceedings, no corresponding accrual has been recorded in the financial statements included in this Form 10-Q. However, a significant judgment against the Company in the Delaware Proceeding, which is currently in trial, would have a material adverse effect on the Company’s business, which could result in the Company needing to curtail or cease operations and seek protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. Any settlement of the Delaware Proceeding or other actions may also have an adverse effect on the Company’s business, financial condition and results of operations, including, but not limited to, substantial expenses, the payment of royalties, licensing or other fees payable to third parties, or restrictions on its ability to develop, manufacture, and sell its products.

steps.text: Indenture §7.06 (Limitation on Suits): "No Holder shall have any right to institute any proceeding, judicial or otherwise, in respect of this Indenture, or for the appointment of a receiver or trustee, or for any other remedy hereunder (other than in the case of an Event of Default specified in clause (j) or (k) of Section 7.01), unless: (a) the Holder of a Note gives to the Trustee written notice of a continuing Event of Default; (b) the Holders of at least 25% in Principal Amount of the then outstanding Notes make a written request to the Trustee to pursue the remedy; (c) such Holder of a Note or Holders of Notes offer and, if requested, provide to the Trustee indemnity reasonably satisfactory to the Trustee against any loss, liability or expense; (d) the Trustee does not comply with the request within 60 days after receipt of the request and the offer and, if requested, the provision of indemnity; and (e) during such 60-day period the Majority Holders do not give the Trustee a direction inconsistent with the request."

Indenture §7.07 (Unconditional Rights of Holders of Notes to Receive Payment): "Notwithstanding any other provision of this Indenture, the right of any Holder to receive payment of the Principal, the Redemption Price, or Interest, in respect of the Notes held by such Holder, on or after the respective due dates expressed in the Notes or any Redemption Date, as applicable, and to convert the Notes in accordance with ARTICLE 9, or to bring suit for the enforcement of any such payment on or after such respective dates or the right to convert, shall not be impaired or affected adversely without the consent of such Holder."
11 U.S.C. §303(b)(1): where the debtor has 12 or more creditors, an involuntary petition is filed by three or more creditors holding noncontingent, undisputed claims above the statutory threshold.

When it is decided: once in each stage of the dispute; paid 30 days after the stage begins
Decision date: P5 16 Jun 2024, median 20 Jun 2024, P95 22 Jun 2024 = when the decision falls, across the simulations that reach it

Settlement offer: P5 $3.2M, median $3.4M = the company's available cash on the settlement date less its 30-day operating need, floored at zero and capped at the amount owed (30-day need: median $2.8M); paid as 12 equal monthly installments, the first on the settlement date (30 days after the decision) and one each month after; the claim is released on the settlement date; installments due after 10 Nov 2024 fall after the analysis period
The notes' judgment default (§7.01(i)) on the judgment as entered: 60 days after execution became available: between 16 Aug 2024 and 22 Aug 2024 (median 20 Aug 2024)

The notes' judgment default (§7.01(i)) if the judgment is final only on the post-trial ruling: 60 days after the court's order on the last pending post-trial motion: between 16 Aug 2024 and 22 Aug 2024 (median 20 Aug 2024)
The deadline to file a notice of appeal: between 16 Jun 2024 and 22 Jun 2024 (median 20 Jun 2024)
The notes' interest payment date: 17 Jun 2024: $1,320,000.00 due, paid in shares
Nasdaq's deadline to regain compliance with the minimum bid price: 21 Oct 2024

On the loan: through the company's cash. Slope debits each installment in full on its due date when the company's available cash covers it; a debit that fails stays past due and is retried on the next due date or month-end. Slope funds a draw only while nothing is overdue and no petition is filed

When it is decided: when the offer is made
Decision date: P5 16 Jun 2024, median 20 Jun 2024, P95 22 Jun 2024 = when the decision falls, across the simulations that reach it

Projected available cash at decision date: P5 $8.7M, median $8.9M = opening cash + projected operating flows from the bank data + the dispute's cash to that date, across the simulations that reach the decision
Amount owed at decision: median $67.8M, highest $67.8M = the judgment on this path (as entered, or as the ruling leaves it) + statutory interest to the decision date - amounts already collected

Settlement offer: P5 $3.2M, median $3.4M = the company's available cash on the settlement date less its 30-day operating need, floored at zero and capped at the amount owed (30-day need: median $2.8M); paid as 12 equal monthly installments, the first on the settlement date (30 days after the decision) and one each month after; the claim is released on the settlement date; installments due after 10 Nov 2024 fall after the analysis period
The notes' judgment default (§7.01(i)) on the judgment as entered: 60 days after execution became available: between 16 Aug 2024 and 22 Aug 2024 (median 20 Aug 2024)

The notes' judgment default (§7.01(i)) if the judgment is final only on the post-trial ruling: 60 days after the court's order on the last pending post-trial motion: between 16 Aug 2024 and 22 Aug 2024 (median 20 Aug 2024)
The deadline to file a notice of appeal: between 16 Jun 2024 and 22 Jun 2024 (median 20 Jun 2024)
The notes' interest payment date: 17 Jun 2024: $1,320,000.00 due, paid in shares
Nasdaq's deadline to regain compliance with the minimum bid price: 21 Oct 2024

On the loan: through the company's cash. Slope debits each installment in full on its due date when the company's available cash covers it; a debit that fails stays past due and is retried on the next due date or month-end. Slope funds a draw only while nothing is overdue and no petition is filed

However, a significant judgment against the Company in the Delaware Proceeding, which is currently in trial, would have a material adverse effect on the Company’s business, which could result in the Company needing to curtail or cease operations and seek protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. Any settlement of the Delaware Proceeding or other actions may also have an adverse effect on the Company’s business, financial condition and results of operations, including, but not limited to, substantial expenses, the payment of royalties, licensing or other fees payable to third parties, or restrictions on its ability to develop, manufacture, and sell its products.

steps.text: Event of Default (§7.01(i)): final money judgments above the threshold, excluding amounts covered by insurance, remain undischarged, unpaid or unstayed for the stated period, during which execution is not effectively stayed; it takes effect on notice by the trustee or holders of 25% of principal.

Acceleration (§7.02): on an Event of Default the trustee or holders of 25% may declare the notes due; a bankruptcy petition makes them due automatically; holders of a majority may rescind once every default is cured, and a judgment default is cured by payment, discharge or a stay.

steps.text: Fed. R. Civ. P. 62(a): "execution on a judgment and proceedings to enforce it are stayed for 30 days after its entry, unless the court orders otherwise."

quotes.quote: As of March 31, 2024, the Company had cash and cash equivalents of $ 15.2 million and working capital of $ 10.3 million. In the absence of additional liquidity, the Company anticipates that its existing cash resources, with a continued focus on cash conservation, is sufficient to fund its operations into the third quarter of fiscal 2025.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: an adverse judgment against the Company in the trial with respect to Qorvo Inc. vs. Akoustis Technologies, Inc. DE Case 1:21-cv-01417-JPM , as described below under Note 14. Commitments and Contingencies (the “Delaware Trial”), would reduce the amount of time that the Company could continue operating with its current cash resources, and create an urgent need for additional liquidity or result in the Company’s curtailing or ceasing operations and seeking protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. These matters raise substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern within one year from the date of this filing.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: as the Company cannot currently predict the results of the proceedings, no corresponding accrual has been recorded in the financial statements included in this Form 10-Q. However, a significant judgment against the Company in the Delaware Proceeding, which is currently in trial, would have a material adverse effect on the Company’s business, which could result in the Company needing to curtail or cease operations and seek protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. Any settlement of the Delaware Proceeding or other actions may also have an adverse effect on the Company’s business, financial condition and results of operations, including, but not limited to, substantial expenses, the payment of royalties, licensing or other fees payable to third parties, or restrictions on its ability to develop, manufacture, and sell its products.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: Except for the $ 48.0 million of common stock remaining available to be sold under its ATM Sales Agreement with Oppenheimer & Co. Inc., Craig-Hallum Capital Group LLC, and Roth Capital Partners, LLC, the Company has no commitments or arrangements to obtain any additional funds, and there can be no assurance such funds will be available on acceptable terms or at all.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: 5,000,000 of the Shares (the “Note Shares”) represent shares that may be issued, at our election, as payment of accrued interest on our 6.0% Convertible Senior Notes due 2027 (the “Notes”), as make-whole payments made in connection with certain conversions of the Notes or as payments made in connection with qualifying fundamental changes of Akoustis Technologies, Inc. (the “Company”)
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies registration statement on Form S-3, 13 May 2024 (resale of note-interest shares)

quotes.quote: Our Common Stock is traded on the Nasdaq Capital Market (“Nasdaq”) under the symbol “AKTS.” On May 10, 2024, the last reported sale price for our Common Stock was $0.57 per share.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies registration statement on Form S-3, 13 May 2024 (resale of note-interest shares)

quotes.quote: The Company’s short-term and long-term liquidity requirements primarily arise from funding (i) research and development expenses, (ii) G&A expenses including salaries, bonuses, and commissions, (iii) working capital requirements, (iv) business acquisitions and investments it may make from time to time, and (v) interest and principal payments related to its $ 44.0 million aggregate principal amount of outstanding convertible notes and $ 4.0 million promissory note. Additionally, the Delaware Trial is currently in process. To the extent that the outcome of the trial includes judgments against the Company for significant damages or other relief, the Company’s liquidity will be additionally and severely constrained.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

steps.text: Event of Default (§7.01(i)): final money judgments above the threshold, excluding amounts covered by insurance, remain undischarged, unpaid or unstayed for the stated period, during which execution is not effectively stayed; it takes effect on notice by the trustee or holders of 25% of principal.

Acceleration (§7.02): on an Event of Default the trustee or holders of 25% may declare the notes due; a bankruptcy petition makes them due automatically; holders of a majority may rescind once every default is cured, and a judgment default is cured by payment, discharge or a stay.

quotes.quote: As of March 31, 2024, the Company had cash and cash equivalents of $ 15.2 million and working capital of $ 10.3 million. In the absence of additional liquidity, the Company anticipates that its existing cash resources, with a continued focus on cash conservation, is sufficient to fund its operations into the third quarter of fiscal 2025.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: an adverse judgment against the Company in the trial with respect to Qorvo Inc. vs. Akoustis Technologies, Inc. DE Case 1:21-cv-01417-JPM , as described below under Note 14. Commitments and Contingencies (the “Delaware Trial”), would reduce the amount of time that the Company could continue operating with its current cash resources, and create an urgent need for additional liquidity or result in the Company’s curtailing or ceasing operations and seeking protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. These matters raise substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern within one year from the date of this filing.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: Except for the $ 48.0 million of common stock remaining available to be sold under its ATM Sales Agreement with Oppenheimer & Co. Inc., Craig-Hallum Capital Group LLC, and Roth Capital Partners, LLC, the Company has no commitments or arrangements to obtain any additional funds, and there can be no assurance such funds will be available on acceptable terms or at all.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: as the Company cannot currently predict the results of the proceedings, no corresponding accrual has been recorded in the financial statements included in this Form 10-Q. However, a significant judgment against the Company in the Delaware Proceeding, which is currently in trial, would have a material adverse effect on the Company’s business, which could result in the Company needing to curtail or cease operations and seek protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. Any settlement of the Delaware Proceeding or other actions may also have an adverse effect on the Company’s business, financial condition and results of operations, including, but not limited to, substantial expenses, the payment of royalties, licensing or other fees payable to third parties, or restrictions on its ability to develop, manufacture, and sell its products.

quotes.quote: an adverse judgment against the Company in the trial with respect to Qorvo Inc. vs. Akoustis Technologies, Inc. DE Case 1:21-cv-01417-JPM , as described below under Note 14. quotes.quote: as the Company cannot currently predict the results of the proceedings, no corresponding accrual has been recorded in the financial statements included in this Form 10-Q. Any settlement of the Delaware Proceeding or other actions may also have an adverse effect on the Company’s business, financial condition and results of operations, including, but not limited to, substantial expenses, the payment of royalties, licensing or other fees payable to third parties, or restrictions on its ability to develop, manufacture, and sell its products.

quotes.quote: As of March 31, 2024, the Company had cash and cash equivalents of $ 15.2 million and working capital of $ 10.3 million. In the absence of additional liquidity, the Company anticipates that its existing cash resources, with a continued focus on cash conservation, is sufficient to fund its operations into the third quarter of fiscal 2025.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: an adverse judgment against the Company in the trial with respect to Qorvo Inc. vs. Akoustis Technologies, Inc. DE Case 1:21-cv-01417-JPM , as described below under Note 14. Commitments and Contingencies (the “Delaware Trial”), would reduce the amount of time that the Company could continue operating with its current cash resources, and create an urgent need for additional liquidity or result in the Company’s curtailing or ceasing operations and seeking protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. These matters raise substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern within one year from the date of this filing.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: as the Company cannot currently predict the results of the proceedings, no corresponding accrual has been recorded in the financial statements included in this Form 10-Q. However, a significant judgment against the Company in the Delaware Proceeding, which is currently in trial, would have a material adverse effect on the Company’s business, which could result in the Company needing to curtail or cease operations and seek protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. Any settlement of the Delaware Proceeding or other actions may also have an adverse effect on the Company’s business, financial condition and results of operations, including, but not limited to, substantial expenses, the payment of royalties, licensing or other fees payable to third parties, or restrictions on its ability to develop, manufacture, and sell its products.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: The Company’s short-term and long-term liquidity requirements primarily arise from funding (i) research and development expenses, (ii) G&A expenses including salaries, bonuses, and commissions, (iii) working capital requirements, (iv) business acquisitions and investments it may make from time to time, and (v) interest and principal payments related to its $ 44.0 million aggregate principal amount of outstanding convertible notes and $ 4.0 million promissory note. Additionally, the Delaware Trial is currently in process. To the extent that the outcome of the trial includes judgments against the Company for significant damages or other relief, the Company’s liquidity will be additionally and severely constrained.

Acceleration (§7.02): on an Event of Default the trustee or holders of 25% may declare the notes due; a bankruptcy petition makes them due automatically; holders of a majority may rescind once every default is cured, and a judgment default is cured by payment, discharge or a stay.

Qorvo sued Akoustis in federal court in Delaware on {commenced} for trade-secret misappropriation, patent infringement and related claims. The jury trial began on {trial_started}; on the review date it is still under way, and the company expects a verdict within days. Nothing is owed until a judgment is entered.
Before trial Qorvo itemised {claim} of damages, almost all of it one measure: the unjust enrichment of a head start built on its trade secrets.

Akoustis holds about {cash} of cash and owes {notes} on convertible notes. A final judgment above {threshold} left unpaid and unstayed for {days} days is a default under the notes, which lets the noteholders demand repayment. Its shares trade below the exchange's minimum bid price; the compliance deadline is {listing}.

assumptions.label: Central setting
assumptions.basis: Settings every path shares (spec §16.3). Central: the feed's historical continuation, no financing, a 30-day cash floor, and Slope's automatic debit (collected in full when cash covers the installment). Each scenario changes one setting and states its basis.

assumptions.label: The announced 30% cut in operating burn
assumptions.basis: Earnings call of 13 May 2024 (CFO): aggressive expense reduction and cost-saving measures, as well as pursuing the investment tax credits, 'all of which we estimate will reduce our operating cash flow burn rate by an additional 30% sequentially in the June quarter'. The March quarter's operating burn was USD 7,791,000; 30% of it is taken off every operating outflow except the litigation-spend proxy and debt service (14,092,000 in the March quarter), a 16.59% cut, from the day after the review to the horizon, so the June quarter's operating burn at the March run rate is about 30% below the March quarter's (USD 7.8M, itself 31% below December). Opex guided to USD 10-11M a quarter is an accrual figure and is not used. The call does not split the tax-credit refund from the cost cuts, so the whole 30% is read as lower outflows; revenue stays on its own path (guided flat to down 5%).

assumptions.label: A USD 5.0M equity injection on 14 Jun 2024
assumptions.basis: A declared scenario, not the record: a plain equity injection of USD 5.0M booked on 14 Jun 2024, one month after the review. On 14 May the company was re-activating its at-the-market program (ATM Sales Agreement of 2 May 2022, USD 48.0M remaining, 10-Q of 13 May 2024); the agents have no obligation to sell, so the program fixes no amount or date. Usable capacity is probably limited by the baby-shelf cap (about one third of public float per 12 months, net of the January raise: roughly USD 9.7M, an inference, not stated before the cutoff); USD 5.0M sits inside it. The central case books no financing.

assumptions.label: USD 5.0M of equity can be raised at the cash floor without an adverse judgment (central USD 9.7M)
assumptions.basis: Owen, item 1 (27 Sep 2026). With no adverse money judgment on the path (no award, or the lower award): the ATM's likely usable capacity under the baby-shelf cap, USD 9.7M. An inference: one third of public float per 12 months, net of the January 2024 USD 10M raise. Record: the ATM (Sales Agreement of 2 May 2022) re-activated on 13 May 2024 with USD 48.0M remaining, and the agents are not obliged to sell (10-Q of 13 May 2024; 424B5 of 2 May 2022 and 29 Jan 2024). Sensitivity: USD 5.0M.

assumptions.label: USD 5.0M of equity can still be raised at the cash floor after an adverse judgment (central none)
assumptions.basis: Owen, item 1 (27 Sep 2026). After a judgment on the claimant's theory: nothing through the ATM. The baby-shelf cap falls with the share price, and the 10-Q (13 May 2024) says an adverse judgment creates 'an urgent need for additional liquidity'. Sensitivity: a distressed raise of USD 5.0M.

assumptions.label: A settlement is paid at once, not over 12 months
assumptions.basis: Owen, 28 Sep 2026. The settlement amount, the company's available cash above its 30-day operating need on the settlement date capped at the amount claimed or owed, bounds what can be paid (spec §16.3). Base: that amount in 12 equal monthly installments, the first on the settlement date. A distressed company does not pay out its runway at once. Installments due after 10 Nov 2024 fall outside the horizon. Sensitivity: the same amount as one lump sum on the settlement date.

assumptions.label: The borrower keeps 30 days of operating need back before paying Slope
assumptions.basis: A borrower-behaviour sensitivity (spec §16.3 Collection): the borrower keeps its next 30 days of operating need back from Slope, so Slope collects min(owed, max(0, available - need)). Slope's mechanism is the automatic debit on each due date (the central case); this is an assumption about the borrower, not the product.

assumptions.label: The cash floor at 60 days of operating need
assumptions.basis: The cash floor at 60 days of operating need instead of 30 (the one alternative setting): the company's cash-floor decision, Jev's cash facts and settlement and stay capacity read it. Collections are unchanged (Slope's debit does not read the floor).

assumptions.label: The lower verdict branch at USD 9,999,999
assumptions.basis: Owen, O1 (27 Sep 2026): the lower J1 branch is liability without the head-start measure. Base: the claimant's own figures for a verdict that rejects that measure, patent USD 279,808 plus corrective advertising USD 1,146,604 = USD 1,426,412 (D.I. 543-1 Ex. A.2 ¶¶19, 42). The poaching USD 809,772 is a UDTPA claim, and D.I. 590 (14 May 2024) held the jury has no basis for compensable UDTPA damages, so it is excluded. The same USD 1,426,412 is the declared bound: where the agent's record leaves a counted component's amount unknown, the branch uses it, labelled as the bound. Sensitivity: USD 9,999,999, the most an award can be and stay below the notes' USD 10.0M threshold.

assumptions.label: The June notes coupon paid in cash
assumptions.basis: The 15 Jun 2024 coupon, USD 1.32M, paid Mon 17 Jun. Indenture §16.02(c): paid in shares unless the company elects cash. The resale S-3 of 13 May 2024 registers 5,000,000 Note Shares for interest and make-whole payments; at USD 0.60 (close, 1 May 2024; 10-Q) the coupon needs about 2.3M shares, inside the registered 5.0M and the 11,403,332 cap. Base: all shares, no cash. Sensitivity: all cash.
